org.name: Front Range Tool Library
org.tagline: Borrow the tool. Skip the shed.
org.mission: We lend tools the way a library lends books. A membership costs less than one weekend rental and gets you access to more than 900 tools, from drills to tile saws to a cider press. We exist so that fixing, building and growing things is affordable for everyone in Longmont.
org.about:
The Tool Library opened in 2016 in a donated garage bay with 140 tools. Today it runs out of a warehouse on 3rd Avenue with two paid staff and about thirty regular volunteers.

Members check out up to five tools for a week at a time. Repair nights on the first Thursday of the month are free and open to non-members: bring a broken thing and someone will help you fix it.

copy.audience: Renters and homeowners in Longmont who need a tool once, people on a budget who want to fix rather than replace, and gardeners who need the big stuff once a season.
keyMessages: More than 900 tools for one annual membership

testimonials.quote: I tiled my bathroom for the price of the tile. The saw was here waiting for me.
testimonials.name: Ana R.

posts.title: Cider press season is here
posts.body: The two cider presses are back from maintenance and can be reserved from September 15th. Members can book them for two days at a time. Bring your own apples and jugs; we have a few crates of windfalls from the Sunset Street orchard for anyone who wants them.

events.title: Repair night
events.description: Bring something broken. Lamps, toasters, bikes, chairs, jeans. Free and open to everyone.

events.title: Volunteer orientation
events.description: An hour's walk-through of the checkout desk and the tool wall. No experience needed.
